---
title: "Simulation Framework Guide"
format: html
---

This document explains the conventions, file structure, and workflow
for the simulation studies under `quarto/simulations/`. It is the
canonical reference for how a single configuration is built,
executed, and consumed — and how multiple configurations are
compared.

# Philosophy {#sec-philosophy}

Three ideas shape the design.

**1. Simulation is code; results are artifacts.** Every simulation
configuration is fully described by a small set of files under
version control. Running those files produces a single `.rds`
bundle that contains both the inputs (DGM, parameters) and the
outputs (per-replicate results). Rendering the article consumes
the bundle.

**2. The article is both runner and tutorial.** The qmd produces
the simulation bundle (in `full` mode) and renders the consumption
view (in any mode). A single source of truth, executed via Quarto's
chunk-rendering machinery — which avoids the stdout-capture
bottleneck that affects standalone Rscript-launched parallel jobs.

**3. The article remains a self-contained tutorial.** Even when a
bundle exists, data preparation, DGM calibration, and a single-trial
sanity check always run inline so the narrative is intact. Only the
expensive `foreach` loops are skipped in import mode.

# Naming Convention {#sec-naming}

```
{study}_{outcome}_{dgm}_{objective}_{focus}_{fsparms}.{ext}
```

| Token       | Examples                              | Notes |
|-------------|---------------------------------------|-------|
| `study`     | `actg175`, `gbsg`                     | study source |
| `outcome`   | `binary`, `survival`, `continuous`, `counts` | outcome type |
| `dgm`       | `m1`, `m2`                            | data-generating model id |
| `objective` | `harm`, `benefit`                     | `sg_objective` axis |
| `focus`     | `hrMaxSG`, `hrMinSG`                  | `sg_focus` criterion |
| `fsparms`   | `fs1`, `fs2`                          | FS parameter bundle |

Example stem:

```
actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1
```

This stem is shared by the per-config article (`.qmd`) and its
saved bundle (`.rds`).

A `simulation_registry.yml` sidecar (optional, future) can map
each token to its full definition (DGM parameters, FS parameter
bundle contents, etc.) so the filenames stay short while the
codes remain self-documenting.

## The "All" sentinel {#sec-all-sentinel}

Cross-cut summaries replace the varied dimension(s) with `All`. The
sentinel can replace one dimension (single-axis cross-cut) or
multiple dimensions (multi-axis cross-cut, via
`expand.grid()` over the relevant level vectors):

| File stem                                              | Varies         | Compares |
|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------|----------|
| `actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fsAll_summary`        | focus × fs     | sg_focus × FS bundle grid |
| `actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fsAll_summary`         | `fs*`          | FS bundles (fixed focus) |
| `actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fs1_summary`          | `focus`        | sg_focus (fixed FS) |
| `actg175_binary_mAll_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1_summary`         | `dgm`          | DGMs |
| `actg175_outcomeAll_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1_summary`       | outcome        | endpoint types |
| `studyAll_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1_summary`          | study          | studies |

Within-study summaries (those with a fixed `study` token) live in
the study's own `_summaries/` subdirectory. Cross-study summaries
(starting with `studyAll_`) live in the top-level
`quarto/simulations/_summaries/`.

# Directory Layout {#sec-layout}

```
quarto/simulations/
  README.qmd                                             ← this file
  _summaries/                                            ← cross-study cross-cuts (later)
    studyAll_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1_summary.qmd
    ...
  actg175/                                               ← per-study dir
    _summaries/                                          ← within-study cross-cuts
      actg175_binary_m1_harm_focusAll_fsAll_summary.qmd
      ...
    _fsparams/                                           ← canonical FS bundle definitions
      fs1_params.R                                       ← used by all *_fs1 qmds
      fs2_params.R                                       ← (future) used by all *_fs2 qmds
    actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1.qmd               ← per-config article (source)
    actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1.rds               ← bundle (artifact, built in full mode)
    actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1.html              ← rendered preview
    actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1_files/            ← Quarto figures
    logs/                                                ← optional log redirects (Rscript-based renders)
  gbsg/                                                  ← future studies
    _summaries/
    _fsparams/
    ...
```

# The Two-File Pattern {#sec-files}

Every configuration consists of two files sharing a stem.

```
              ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │   <stem>.qmd     (per-config article)    │
              │   tutorial + simulation runner            │
              │   data prep + DGM cal + foreach loops +  │
              │   bundle save (full mode) + OC rendering │
              └────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                               │ produces (in full mode)
                               │ consumes (in import / auto mode)
                               ▼
              ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │   <stem>.rds     (bundle / artifact)     │
              │   meta + dgm + results                   │
              └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## `<stem>.qmd` — per-config article {#sec-article}

A **self-contained tutorial-and-runner** for the configuration.
Always runs:

- Setup (libraries, parameters)
- Data preparation
- DGM calibration (H1) + null construction (H0)
- Single-trial sanity check (one simulated trial, FS analysis,
  small tables)
- Operating-characteristics tables and plots

Conditionally runs (only when `sim_mode != "import"`):

- Parallel plan setup
- H1 and H0 `foreach` loops at the configured N

Conditionally runs (only when `sim_mode == "full"`):

- Save bundle chunk: assembles the meta/dgm/results structure
  and `saveRDS()`s to `BUNDLE_PATH`

A single mode-handoff chunk routes between import (load bundle)
and demo/full (use just-computed results), then downstream chunks
are mode-agnostic.

# FS Parameter Bundles {#sec-fsparams}

Each `fs*` token names a **shared parameter bundle**. To keep
parameter values consistent across the multiple `sg_focus`
configurations that share an `fs*` label, the canonical values
live in a single file under `_fsparams/`:

```
quarto/simulations/<study>/_fsparams/
  fs1_params.R     ← used by all *_fs1 qmds in this study
  fs2_params.R     ← (future) used by all *_fs2 qmds
```

Each file defines a single function (`get_fs1_params()`,
`get_fs2_params()`, ...) that returns the FS parameter list. The
per-config qmd sources the file and calls the function:

```r
source("_fsparams/fs1_params.R")
fs_params <- get_fs1_params(sg_focus = fs_sg_focus)
```

The returned `fs_params` is used directly — no overrides in the
qmd. The function internally applies any `sg_focus`-dependent
package constraints (e.g., `stop_threshold` is returned as `NULL`
when `sg_focus` is `"hrMaxSG"` or `"hrMinSG"`).

Why the split:

- **One source of truth per `fs*` bundle**: editing `c1` once in
  `fs1_params.R` propagates to all five `*_fs1.qmd` files at next
  render. No manual cross-file edits.
- **Documentation lives next to values**: each `fs*_params.R` file
  has a header comment describing the regime — what makes `fs1`
  different from `fs2`, what's it tuned for. Self-maintaining.
- **No qmd-level parameter knowledge**: the qmd doesn't know or
  care what's in the bundle; it just sources, calls, uses. To
  change a parameter, you edit one file (`fs*_params.R`).

## `<stem>.rds` — bundle {#sec-bundle}

The artifact produced by the article (in `full` mode) and consumed
by the article (in `import` / `auto` mode) and by cross-cut summaries.

Schema:

```
list(
  meta = list(
    config_id, timestamp, n_alt, n_null, sim_n,
    confounders, fs_params, grf_params,
    diag_keep, diag_keep_first_n,
    t_alt_sec, t_null_sec,
    n_failed_alt, n_failed_null,
    package_version, sessionInfo
  ),
  dgm = list(
    calibrated,    # from calibrate_glm_interaction()
    null           # from generate_glm_dgm(model = "null")
  ),
  results = list(
    alt,           # data.frame from collect_results(); attr(., "n_failed")
    null           # data.frame from collect_results(); attr(., "n_failed")
  )
)
```

The DGMs are stored alongside the results so OC tables that take
`dgm = ...` arguments can be rendered from the bundle alone, with
no need to re-calibrate.

# The Three Render Modes {#sec-modes}

The per-config article supports four modes via the `sim_mode`
constant in its setup chunk:

| Mode      | Behavior | When to use |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| `import`  | Load `.rds` bundle; skip `foreach` loops; use bundle's DGM and results for downstream rendering | After a `full`-mode render has produced the bundle. Fastest. |
| `demo`    | Run small-N inline simulations (default 100 + 100). Does not save a bundle. | First-time exploration; quick interactive check. |
| `full`    | Run production-N inline simulations and **save bundle** to `BUNDLE_PATH`. | Production runs. Render via `quarto render` from the terminal. |
| `auto`    | `import` if `BUNDLE_PATH` exists, else `demo`. | Default. Sensible for most workflows. |

In `import` mode, the freshly-built DGM objects (from the always-
running calibration chunks) are **overridden** by the bundle's
DGMs. This guarantees the OC tables reference the same DGM that
produced the imported results — preventing subtle inconsistencies
if the user's working DGM-construction code drifts from when the
bundle was built.

# Cross-cut Summaries {#sec-summaries}

Cross-cut summaries live in two places, depending on what varies:

- **Within-study** summaries (study fixed, other tokens vary):
  `quarto/simulations/<study>/_summaries/`. Most summaries are
  this kind, since within-study comparisons are typically the
  primary analytical target.
- **Cross-study** summaries (study itself varies — `studyAll_*`):
  `quarto/simulations/_summaries/`. Defer until needed.

A typical summary article:

1. Declares level vectors for each varied dimension
   (e.g., `focus_levels`, `fs_levels`)
2. Builds `configs` via `expand.grid()` over those vectors;
   constructs `config_id`, `label`, and `bundle_path` per row
3. Filters to existing bundles (with a `strict_bundles` flag for
   completeness checks)
4. Reads each bundle
5. Validates that `meta$config_id` matches what's declared
6. Extracts per-config metrics (detection rate, FPR, mean |Ĥ|,
   median ÔR(Ĥ), Sens/Spec/PPV/NPV)
7. Renders side-by-side `gt` comparison tables (`groupname_col`
   on `analysis`; varied dimensions become row identifiers)
8. Renders comparison plots — for two varied dimensions, typically
   `x = <primary>, fill = <secondary>` with dodging

To add a configuration to an existing summary, append a level to
the relevant vector and re-render. Missing cells in the
`expand.grid` are skipped automatically (or error if
`strict_bundles <- TRUE`).

The `focusAll_fsAll_summary` template assumes a **shared truth**
across bundles (same study × outcome × DGM × objective).
Templates that vary the DGM need per-bundle reference annotations
(e.g., a target OR per facet rather than a single dashed line).

# Adding a New Configuration {#sec-adding}

## Adding a new `sg_focus` (existing `fs*` bundle)

For a new `sg_focus` value within an existing `fs*` bundle (e.g.,
adding `actg175_binary_m1_harm_minSG_fs1` to a project where
`fs1` already exists):

1. **Decide the focus token.** Make sure it's distinct from
   existing focus tokens in the directory.

2. **Use `clone_config.sh`** to clone from the closest existing
   focus config:

   ```bash
   ./quarto/simulations/clone_config.sh hrMaxSG minSG
   ```

   Token replacement happens automatically across all references.

3. **No further qmd edits needed for the `fs*` parameters.** The
   `_fsparams/fs1_params.R` file already encodes any `sg_focus`-
   dependent rules (e.g., `stop_threshold` is returned as `NULL`
   automatically when `sg_focus` is `hrMaxSG` or `hrMinSG`).

4. **Render in `full` mode** to produce the bundle:

   ```bash
   # Edit the setup chunk: sim_mode <- "full"
   quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_minSG_fs1.qmd
   ```

5. **Switch back to `auto`** in the setup chunk.

6. **Add to applicable cross-cut summaries.** Append `"minSG"`
   to `focus_levels` in `_summaries/...focusAll_fsAll_summary.qmd`.

## Adding a new `fs*` bundle (across all `sg_focus` values)

This is the more powerful pattern. With one new file in
`_fsparams/`, you can spawn a full set of `sg_focus` configs that
share the new parameter values.

For a hypothetical `fs2` bundle:

1. **Define `fs2`** by creating its parameter file:

   ```bash
   cd quarto/simulations/actg175/_fsparams/
   cp fs1_params.R fs2_params.R
   ```

   Edit `fs2_params.R`:
   - Rename the function: `get_fs1_params` → `get_fs2_params`
   - Update the header comment to describe what makes `fs2` different
   - Edit the parameter values that distinguish `fs2` from `fs1`

2. **Clone each `sg_focus` qmd** to the `fs2` token:

   ```bash
   for focus in hr hrMaxSG hrMinSG maxSG minSG; do
     cp actg175_binary_m1_harm_${focus}_fs1.qmd \
        actg175_binary_m1_harm_${focus}_fs2.qmd
     # Then edit each new qmd to update fs1 -> fs2 references
   done
   ```

   (A future `clone_config.sh` enhancement will handle this loop
   plus the in-file token replacement.)

3. **Edit each new qmd**: update the `source()` line to point at
   `fs2_params.R`, the function call to `get_fs2_params(...)`, and
   any references to the old `fs1` token (BUNDLE_PATH, validation
   strings, intro text).

4. **Render each in `full` mode** to produce the bundles. Can be
   parallelized across machines.

5. **Add to cross-cut summaries**: append `"fs2"` to
   `fs_levels` in the relevant summary qmd.

## A new study or outcome

If the new configuration introduces a new study or outcome, also:

- Create the study directory: `mkdir -p quarto/simulations/{study}/`
- Create `quarto/simulations/{study}/_fsparams/` and define your
  `fs*_params.R` file(s) for the new study (FS parameters often
  differ across studies/outcomes due to sample sizes, base rates,
  etc.)
- Be prepared to adapt the data prep + calibration sections —
  they're study-specific and can't be copy-pasted from `actg175`.

# Operational Notes {#sec-ops}

## Git tracking

Both `.html` previews (alongside the `.qmd`) and `.rds` bundles
are tracked in version control. Bundles are deliberately tracked
because:

- Simulations are expensive to recompute
- Bundles are part of the reproducibility story (a result tied to
  a `git_sha`)
- The pkgdown site can be built from cached bundles without
  re-running simulations

## CRAN compliance

The entire `quarto/` tree is excluded from the package tarball via
`^quarto$` in `.Rbuildignore`. None of the simulation infrastructure
ships to CRAN.

## Parallel plan

Use `multisession` for cross-platform compatibility:

- **Linux**: `multicore` works, but `multisession` works equally
  well and avoids divergent behavior across platforms.
- **macOS**: `multicore` silently falls back to `sequential` in
  RStudio. `multisession` works correctly.

Inside each `foreach` worker, the code calls
`future::plan("sequential")` to prevent nested parallelism (the
package's internal subgroup search is not parallelized at this
layer).

## Logging

Two reasonable patterns:

1. **RStudio Render button or Console** — Quarto streams progress to
   the Render pane. The `#| output: false` chunk option on the
   foreach loops keeps the output volume manageable. No log file.
   Default for interactive development.

2. **Shell redirection** — for headless / scheduled runs:
   ```bash
   quarto render quarto/simulations/actg175/actg175_binary_m1_harm_hrMaxSG_fs1.qmd \
     > quarto/simulations/actg175/logs/render_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log 2>&1
   ```
   The `logs/` directory under each study dir is gitignored
   by convention.

The qmd does not configure file-based logging itself — that
decision is left to the caller.

## Reproducibility

Each `foreach` loop uses
`.options.future = list(seed = TRUE)` for L'Ecuyer-CMRG streams.
Set the master seed once via `set.seed()` in the article's setup
chunk. Re-running with the same seed and the same package version
produces identical bundles.

The bundle records `package_version`. Discrepancies between the
recorded version and the current installed version are a signal
to re-run.

# Quick Reference {#sec-quickref}

| Action                                | Command / file |
|--------------------------------------|----------------|
| Build a bundle (production)          | Set `sim_mode <- "full"` in qmd; `quarto render <stem>.qmd` |
| Render per-config article (auto)     | `quarto render <stem>.qmd` (with `sim_mode <- "auto"`) |
| Force inline demo (small N, no save) | Set `sim_mode <- "demo"` in qmd setup |
| Compare configs                      | Edit `configs` in summary qmd; render |
| Inspect a bundle's metadata          | `readRDS("<stem>.rds")$meta` |
